title: Rain Washes Out Bengaluru Decider as India and West Indies Draw T20 Series 2-2
excerpt: India were 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs of a nine-over game when rain ended Chinnaswamy's first international in two years, ending India's 12-series home winning streak.
body:
• Rain abandoned the fifth T20I in Bengaluru with India 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs, leaving the five-match series drawn 2-2.
  • The match, Chinnaswamy Stadium's first international in two years, was cut to nine overs a side after a two-and-a-half-hour delay, then washed out before a five-over West Indies chase of 84 could start by the 10:21 pm cut-off.
  • Ishan Kishan hit 30 off 10 balls and Naman Dhir an unbeaten 24 off 6; India also recorded their fastest team fifty in men's T20Is, in 2.5 overs.
  • The draw ends India's 12-series winning streak at home and denies West Indies a first series win in India since 2002.

India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series after rain washed out the deciding fifth game in Bengaluru on Saturday, Reuters reported. The match was abandoned at 10:16 pm with India 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs.

A Nine-Over Game That Never Finished

Persistent drizzle delayed the scheduled 6:30 pm toss by about two hours, according to IANS. When play finally began at 9:15 pm, the match had been reduced to nine overs a side. West Indies captain Shai Hope won the toss and chose to field.

India lost Abhishek Sharma for six to Keemo Paul, but Ishan Kishan hammered 30 off 10 balls, taking 24 runs from one Romario Shepherd over. India reached their fifty in 2.5 overs, their fastest team fifty in men's T20I cricket. Naman Dhir added an unbeaten 24 off six balls before Shamar Springer bowled Tilak Varma in the eighth over and the rain returned for good.

With no possibility of a five-over West Indies chase of 84 before the 10:21 pm cut-off, the umpires called the match off and the players exchanged handshakes in the dressing rooms.

What the Draw Means

The washout ends India's run of 12 straight home series wins, a streak lasting four years. It also denies West Indies a first series victory in India since 2002, after a tour on which they competed fiercely across the ODIs and the T20s. Hope finished the series as its leading run-scorer with 261 runs.

There was one more anticlimax. Veteran seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar, recalled to India's T20 squad for the first time since November 2022, was named in the XI but never bowled a ball.

A Flat End to Chinnaswamy's Return

The fixture was the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium's first international match in two years, and a crowd that had waited patiently through hours of drizzle got 7.4 overs for its patience. The forecast had offered hope in the morning, when the rain probability fell from 70% to 30%, but the evening drizzle never cleared long enough.

What's Next

India's attention turns to the New Zealand tour, with squad questions over bowling depth still open. West Indies leave India without the series win, but with a drawn T20 series against the world's strongest home side as evidence of progress.
